title: SchemeTorsorPullbackEquivariantHomIsIso
statement: Let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $M$ a finite abelian group, and $t$ a scheme $M$-torsor over $Y$ [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor]. Set $G=\underline M_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $R$ be any $i^{-1}G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $f:i^{-1}_{\rm set}(t.\mathrm{sheaf})\to R.\mathrm{sheaf}$ any morphism of sheaves of sets. Suppose $f(\eta_T(g+\!_v x))=\eta_G(g)+\!_v f(\eta_T(x))$ over $W\times_Y Y_0$ for every $W\in Y_{\acute et}$, $g\in G(W)$ and $x\in t.\mathrm{sheaf}(W)$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism. This statement does not construct $f$, and assumes no scheme representative for $R$.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (2), (4); Tag 0A5G; Cohomology on Sites Section 03AG

proof.text: Apply the inverse-image clause of etale_torsor_h1_functoriality to t.toSheafTorsor. Obtain a torsor T for upperStar G, an isomorphism e from the set inverse image to T.sheaf, and its unit-action compatibility. Define the morphism q = e.inv composed with f. Only the inverse-image construction clause is used, not the cohomology equality or contracted-product clause.

For a destination-site coefficient section a and torsor section x, apply etaleInverseImage_joint_representatives to a and e.inv(x). On its covering sieve, write both sections as restrictions of units over one source object. Naturality of e turns the representative of e.inv(x) into one of x. The unit-action compatibility of e and the hypothesis on f prove the equivariance identity for q on these unit images, cancelling e with its inverse. Naturality of q and the actions gives equivariance on every member of the covering sieve. Separatedness of R.sheaf gives the identity globally.
Use Torsor.Iso.ofHom q with the full equivariance just established to obtain IsIso q. Since f = e.hom composed with q, composition of isomorphisms gives IsIso f.
